Closest verified precedents are GRU-D and time-aware T-GRU: both attenuate the previous state before the recurrent update. GRU-D uses \(\bar h_{t-1}=\gamma_t\odot h_{t-1}\), with \(\gamma_t=\exp[-\max(0,W_\gamma\delta_t+b_\gamma)]\); T-GRU uses scalar time decay \(\bar h_{t-1}=g(\Delta t)h_{t-1}\). These establish prior state-decay mechanisms, but neither establishes the exact item-content-conditioned scalar proposal \(h_t=\mathrm{GRU}(x_t,\alpha(x_t)h_{t-1})\). They originate outside recommendation. [GRU-D](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-24271-9.pdf), [T-GRU](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12911-021-01662-z).

Using update-fraction convention, standard GRU computes \(r,u=\sigma(Wx+Uh+b)\), \(n=\tanh(W_nx+U_n(r\odot h)+b_n)\), then \(h'=(1-u)\odot h+u\odot n\). Reset gates affect candidate construction; update gates couple retention and writing. Pre-scaling replaces every occurrence of \(h\) with \(\alpha h\), changing both gates, candidate and carry path; therefore it is not generally equivalent to either existing gate. Recommendation precedent DIEN instead uses AGRU, \(h'=(1-a)h+an\), or AUGRU, replacing \(u\) by \(au\); AIGRU scales the input. These are related attention mechanisms, not complete-update state pre-scaling. [DIEN](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/4545/4423).

Proposed controls: ordinary GRU (\(\alpha=1\)); validation-tuned fixed retention \(\alpha=c\); jointly learned global scalar \(\alpha=\sigma(b)\); and a capacity control routing the same gate network into an additive input correction, with equal active trainable parameter count. A shuffled-conditioning variant preserves gate capacity while disrupting content alignment. Retrain each variant separately with identical seeds, splits and training budgets; select by macro validation HR@10. Each variant uses exactly one jointly trained network/checkpoint per category, without score fusion. These are proposed ablations, not reported findings.
